narrative_purpose: Shows why the equator runs hot and the poles cold: identical sunlight strikes the curved world square-on at the equator and at a glancing angle near the pole, concentrating versus spreading the same energy.
subject: The curved limb of a planet shown from the side as a large arc. Two equal bundles of straight parallel light rays come in from one direction. The upper bundle hits the curve near its middle nearly head-on and lands on a small, intensely bright concentrated patch of glowing surface. The lower bundle strikes the curve near its bottom edge at a shallow grazing angle and smears across a long, dim, stretched-out strip of surface.
scene: Dark space beside the planet's curved edge, soft haze along the limb, the two light bundles drawn as faintly glowing streaks of equal width.
camera: Side-on diagrammatic view of the planetary curve, flat and clear.
light: The concentrated patch glows hot and bright; the smeared strip is faint and cool; the incoming rays carry a soft even glow.
palette: Void-indigo space and dark planetary surface, the concentrated patch warm amber-bright, the smeared strip cool dim teal, rays pale misty-cyan.
style: Painterly plate that reads as a diagram through composition alone, soft glowing forms, NOT a hard vector chart, NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: Moderate: clear contrast between the small bright patch and the long dim strip; soft painterly edges, no hard outlines.
composition: The planet's curve filling one side, two equal ray bundles entering, the bright concentrated patch high and the dim stretched strip low, so the eye compares the two footprints directly.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette; warm amber used only to mark the concentrated equatorial heat. Reads as a teaching picture, not an annotated figure.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no angle symbols, no rulers, no grid, no diagram chrome, no 3D-render or photographic look
